quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal in the direction you want to move. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one else is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The maximum or minimum speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed to drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum speed you can legally drive on a road when conditions are ideal. You may drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and when bad weather or road construction makes the posted speed unsafe.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle immediately. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary, but try to stop heavy bleeding with pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles to arrive.

questions.question: When driving at night with oncoming traffic, your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when meeting or following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone on the road safe.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for the traffic to pass before turning. If the light is green and no vehicle ahead is turning left, you may enter the intersection to prepare for your left turn.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without emergency stops. This helps prevent the driver behind you from hitting your vehicle.

questions.question: A vehicle is entering the freeway from an entrance ramp into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Honk your horn so they see you.
Change lanes or slow down to give them space.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to give them space.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. Change lanes when possible to let them merge safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want it to go. As soon as the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: The right lane is ending. Traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An upcoming intersection.
Road construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending. Traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane will end ahead. Drivers in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a pedestrian crossing is coming. Be careful and watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: When another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane is available, wait until the road ahead is clear. Then slow down gradually to encourage the other driver to pass you.
Never slow down suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane exists, move over. If no right lane is available, wait until the road is clear ahead, then slow down gradually. This lets the other driver pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: What speed is best for the area.
The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive.
What speed to drive in heavy traffic.
What speed to drive in bad conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum speed allowed on that road. The posted limits are for good conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and easily.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and easily.
questions.explanation: When someone wants to pass you, slow down. This creates space in front of you so the other driver can pass more safely and quickly.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line divide the road, and the broken line is on your side, you may pass if:

options.text: It is an emergency.
You are on an expressway.
There is no oncoming traffic.
You are at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is on your side of the road, you may pass if the road ahead is clear of oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: A seat belt should be fastened so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Is tucked under the seat.
Silences the seat belt warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable, with space for your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Before turning left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Look for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before a left turn, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Wait for oncoming traffic and pedestrians to clear, then turn.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the highest posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When it rains heavily and you cannot see clearly, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If the rain is too heavy, pull over and stop until it clears.

questions.question: The most important thing to remember about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may be hard to control in a curve because of its forward motion. To stay in control, slow down before entering the curve.

questions.question: You notice the driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Give the vehicle extra space.
Know that the driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Do not copy this driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to have an accident.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has several turns or curves.
Traffic will increase ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, drive slower, do not brake or turn suddenly, and stay farther away from the car ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
Workers are ahead on the road.
A side road is ahead.
A playground is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about dangers ahead. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when following a truck. On a hill with limited sight, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only if other vehicles yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When you are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can get all the way across without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can get all the way across without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:

options.text: Leaving extra time to reach your destination.
Following posted speed limits.
Using turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and give yourself plenty of time to reach your destination.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and use extra caution around children. They may not understand danger and may run in front of you without looking.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
The road ahead turns sharply. Slow down.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply. Slow down.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a sharp turn. Slow down before you reach the curve, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if you need to.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for all vehicles and pedestrians to clear before you go.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes because other vehicles could hit you. Turn off engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross quickly without stopping.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By looking straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that mirrors cannot show. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your ability to judge speed and distance gets worse.
You become less alert.
You stay calm and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stay calm and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you concentrate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: You must pull over for an emergency vehicle:

options.text: No matter which direction you are traveling.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must pull to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and signals. Remember that trains, cars, and bicycles all share the road.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. You should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to let them return to the right lane easily and safely.

questions.question: In bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination quickly.
Stay closer to the car ahead.
Stay farther away from the car ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: Driving ability can be harmed by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Alcohol, medications, and drowsiness can all harm your ability to drive.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Let other road users know what you are doing.
Pay no attention to other drivers.
Drive only on back roads.
Avoid driving during busy times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other road users know what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Tell other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do by using your signals when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at:

options.text: Curves and hills.
Churches and schools.
Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
Freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the road on the right side and let traffic pass.
Block other cars from passing.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road on the right side and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, pull off and let other vehicles pass. Only drive much slower than the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn allowed.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to drive in your current direction.

questions.question: Signaling before you turn, change lanes, or pull away from a curb:

options.text: Is only needed when other cars are near.
Is a good habit and the law requires it.
Is only needed during the move, not before.
Is not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or turning. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Making it harder to focus on driving.
Lowering your chances of a crash.
Making you fall asleep while driving.
Making you more aware of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making it harder to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect how well you drive. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can hurt your driving ability. Stress reduces your focus on driving. Wait to drive if you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The full width of a lane like other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The sidewalk width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full width of a lane like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full lane width to stay safe. They are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs show:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you of railroad crossings. Yield to trains and never try to pass a train.
